[← Telecom](../index.qmd)

The antenna and radio hardware side of 5G: what 64 transmit chains buy, how beams are steered and managed, why oscillators matter at mmWave, how power amplifiers limit modulation and neighbours, and what comes next. Six sections, each from the basic idea to the RF detail.

## Sections

::: {.lesson-table .column-page}
| | Section | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Massive MIMO: 64T64R](lectures/01-massive-mimo-64t64r.qmd) | What 64T64R means; array gain and EIRP; uplink combining gain; multi-user MIMO; when 32T or 64T is the right choice |
| 2 | [How Beamforming Works](lectures/02-how-beamforming-works.qmd) | Steering with phase delays; phase per element; analog, digital and hybrid beamforming; array factor, beamwidth and grating lobes |
| 3 | [Beam Management & CSI-RS](lectures/03-beam-management-csi-rs.qmd) | Find, refine, track: P1, P2 and P3; CSI-RS and what the phone reports; codebooks; TCI states and QCL; beam failure recovery |
| 4 | [Phase Noise at mmWave](lectures/04-phase-noise-mmwave.qmd) | What phase noise is; why it grows with frequency; common phase error and inter-carrier interference; why FR2 uses wider subcarrier spacing; PT-RS |
| 5 | [PA, EVM & ACLR](lectures/05-pa-evm-aclr.qmd) | The power amplifier and why it distorts; EVM (signal quality) and ACLR (leakage to neighbours); limits per modulation; PAPR, back-off, CFR and DPD |
| 6 | [5G-Advanced & 6G for RF Engineers](lectures/06-5g-advanced-and-6g.qmd) | The 3GPP roadmap from Rel-18 to Rel-21; topics with RF impact (upper mid-band, sub-band full duplex, AI/ML, sensing, satellites, energy saving); what stays the same |
:::

## How each section works

Every section climbs in three steps, so you can stop where you need to:

1. **Beginner · the idea**: what it is and why it matters, in plain words.
2. **Intermediate · how it works**: the mechanism, with the key numbers.
3. **Advanced · expert depth**: equations, 3GPP clauses and field practice.

Then a short **Practice** slide with exercises (answers in the speaker
notes, press **S**) and the references.

**Previous:** [Chapter 3 · Measuring the Radio](../ch3-measuring-the-radio/index.qmd)
